description.value: The study used functional magnetic resonance imaging to investigate brain activation associated with methamphetamine craving and affective picture viewing in methamphetamine addicts and healthy subjects.

spans.text: The study aimed to explore the abnormal activation of special brain areas associated with methamphetamine craving using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and to reveal the neurobiological basis of addiction.

value: Methamphetamine addicts watching methamphetamine-cue images had significant regional activation in the anterior cingulate cortex, which was not observed in healthy subjects watching such images or in methamphetamine addicts or healthy subjects watching images that evoked happy or sad feelings.

Activation of the anterior cingulate in direct and significant response to methamphetamine-cue images can interfere with emotion; addicts watching craving-cue images had emotional conflicts between desires to take the drug and wish to avoid harm from the drug.

description.value: Functional images were motion-corrected, co-registered to each participant's coplanar anatomical image, normalized to Montreal Neurological Institute space, resampled to 2-mm isotropic voxels, and spatially smoothed with an 8-mm Gaussian kernel before regression analysis.

spans.text: Functional images from each participant were motion-corrected and then co-registered to the coplanar anatomical image from that participant. The images were normalized to the standard (Montreal Neurological Institute) space, and the transformation matrix obtained was applied to the co-registered functional images. These normalized functional images, interpolated to 2-mm isotropic voxels and spatially smoothed with a Gaussian filter (8-mm kernel), were subjected to regression analysis.
